  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, April 9, 2024

  The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of Gardena,
  California, was called to order at 7:00 PM on Tuesday, April 9, 2024, in the Council Chamber at
  City Hall 1700 West 162nd Street, Gardena, California; Mayor Tasha Cerda presiding.

  1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Mark E. Henderson; Council Member Rodney
  G. Tanaka; and Council Member Paulette C. Francis. Council Member Wanda Love was
  not present and was on an excused absence. Other City Officials: City Manager Clint
  Osorio; City Attorney Carmen Vasquez; and Deputy City Clerk Becky Romero. City Clerk
  Mina Semenza was not present and was on an excused absence.
  PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION - None

  2.  CLOSED SESSION - None

  CITY ATTORNEY REPORT OUT OF CLOSED SESSION - None

  3.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Cesar Doratt, Recreation Leader with the City of Gardena’s Recreation & Human Services
  Department, led us in the Pledge of Allegiance. Cesar has lived in Gardena for many years
  and attended Amestoy Elementary & Peary Middle School. His hobbies include swimming,
  hiking, powerlifting and kickboxing. He recently picked up photography and editing for fun.
  Occasionally, he will help with the City’s Recreation Department by taking pictures at City
  events. He currently assists special needs students at George De La Torre Elementary in
  Wilmington.

  4.  INVOCATION

  Reverend Bonnie P. Brandon, of The Church of the Holy Communion, led the Invocation.

  5.  PRESENTATIONS

  10. PLANNING & ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY COMMISSION ACTION SHEET

  10.A APRIL 2, 2024 MEETING
  Environmental Impact Report; General Plan Amendment; Zone Change; Zone
  Text Amendment; Specific Plan; Site Plan Review; Vesting Tentative Map;
  Development Agreement, and Affordable Housing Agreement for the
  Normandie Crossing Specific Plan
  Project Location: 16829, 16835, 16907, and 16911 S. Normandie Avenue, 16964
  Brighton Avenue and 0.43 acre property located at the eastern edge of the specific
  plan area
  Project Applicant: Fred Shaffer and Steve Ludwig – 16911 Normandie Associates,
  LLC

  Commission Action: The Planning Commission made the following actions on this
  item by a 3-0-2 vote, being Commissioners Langley and Wright-Scherr not being
  able to vote because of a conflict:
  •  The Planning Commission approved Resolution No. 4-24, recommending the
  City Council certify an Environmental Impact Report for the purposes of the project.
  •  The Planning Commission approved Resolution No. 5-24, recording the
  Commission’s 2 to 1 vote on recommendation of approving General Plan
  Amendment #3-21. The vote of the Planning Commission does not constitute a
  recommendation of approval for the General Plan amendments.
  • The Planning Commission approved Resolution No. 6-24, recommending the
  City Council deny the project entitlement requests other than the General Plan
  Amendment.

  10.B APRIL 2, 2024 MEETING
  Zone Text Amendment #3-24
  Commission Action: The Planning Commission approved Resolution No. PC 7-24
  recommending that the City Council on adopt Ordinance No.1871 to amend Chapter
  5.52 and Title 18 of the Gardena Municipal Code relating to significant tobacco
  retailers, cigar lounges, and hookah lounges and making a finding that the
  Ordinance is exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)
  (3).

  10.C APRIL 2, 2024 MEETING
  Zone Text Amendment #1-24

  recommending that the City Council to adopt Ordinance No. 1865 amending
  Gardena Municipal Code Chapter 18.60 and Sections 5.08.170, 8.16.030, and
  8.16.050 relating to temporary use permits and temporary evens permits and
  amending section 5.04.160 and 5.04.278 relating to permits and finding the
  Ordinance to be categorically exempt from the provisions of the California
  Environmental Quality Act pursuant to Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) and Section
  15304 as a Minor Alterations to Land.

  City Council Action: No action needed on these items. Each item will be
  brought forth to the Council for review at a future City Council Meeting date.

  These Items were Received and Filed.

  13.B Appeal of the Community Development Director's decision to deny Home-Sharing
  Rental Application #24-006

  Mayor Cerda opened up the Appeal Hearing and went over the procedures. Deputy
  City Clerk Romero gave the Oath to the Appellants, Vera Povetina and Yegor
  Kochetov, and City staff, Community Development Director Greg Tsujiuchi, Building
  Official Mark Berg, and Economic Development Manager Jackie Choi.

  Director Tsujiuchi then presented the case on behalf of the City.

  Mayor Cerda then asked the Appellants to come up to present their case.

  Mayor Cerda asked the Appellants if there was anything they would like to add or
  rebut. She then asked Director Tsujiuchi If there was anything further to present or
  rebut.

  Mayor Cerda asked if anyone had asked to speak on this item and if the Council had
  any comments or questions. There were no public speakers.

  Council Member Francis asked for clarification of what they were not allowed to
  discuss. City Attorney Vasquez replied that there is currently a litigation case that
  Mariya Wrightsman has filed against the City regarding home sharing rentals, and the
  Appellants indicated tonight that they will be joining in on that lawsuit.

  Questions and comments were made by Council Member Francis, Mayor Cerda,
  Mayor Pro Tem Henderson, and Council Member Tanaka, which the Appellants
  responded. Building Official Berg, and Director Tsujiuchi also responded to Council’s
  questions and comments. City Attorney Vasquez commented when Council needed
  clarification.

  It was moved by Council Member Tanaka, and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Henderson and carried by the following roll call vote to hold a hearing, receive
  testimony, and uphold the decision of the Community Development Director to
  deny the Home-Sharing Application (HSP) #24-006 and further directed staff to
  draft a Resolution reflecting the Council’s actions today which shall be
  presented at our next regularly scheduled meeting:

  Ayes:  Council Member Tanaka, Mayor Pro Tem Henderson, Council Member
  Francis, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: Council Member Love

  Mayor Cerda then asked that we move Item 19.A out of order by the following

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  22. COUNCIL REMARKS

  1) MAYOR PRO TEM HENDERSON – Since their last meeting, he had the honor of being
  the moderator for the South Bay Cities Council of Governments General Assembly where
  the topic was AI, Friend, or Foe, in public sector. In speaking with the City Manager
  earlier, he definitely wants to encourage our staff to start figuring out ways on how
  artificial intelligence can help us be more efficient to our offerings to our community. He
  was in a presentation today and shared that a few cities are using AI to handle a lot of
  the rudimentary issues and questions that are addressed by the community which allow
  staff to then spend more time on real complex community issues and they were receiving
  high remarks from the community regards to their responsiveness. He said AI may not
  fit in every department or every function, but it’s something we should start looking at.
  He attended the SCAG Community Economic Housing Development Committee
  meeting, as well as the Regional Council Meeting representing Gardena, Inglewood and
  Hawthrone. At SCAG he had his ICA Board Meeting, E-Board Meeting, he wanted to
  congratulate the Gardena Police Foundation Scholarship recipients, some great work,
  and he wanted to thank the Gardena Police Foundation for providing funding for those
  that are going to be beginning their reticulation journey through college and everything
  so that’s a great opportunity. He attended the 34th Annual Southern California Air Quality
  Management District Air Awards, where he was able to talk to folks about air quality and
  different things in regards to what Gardena can do to start working on our air quality
  because we have been labeled a community that has some air quality issues that we
  need to address. He definitely wanted to say thank you to the City of Gardena for giving
  him the opportunity to be the MC of our Wall That Heals ceremony, recognizing the
  Vietnam veterans, he thinks that’s really important for us to recognize those that made
  the ultimate sacrifice and also acknowledge the families that were impacted by the loss
  of their family member because that hurt and pain never goes away. He also did his
  community and business visits and lastly, he wanted to say thank you to the citizens of
  Gardena for re-electing him for a final term, he realizes we still have more work to do
  and he’s up for the challenge so again, he wants to say thank you and he’s ready to get
  back to work.

  2) COUNCIL MEMBER FRANCIS – Since their last meeting, she attended the Martin
  Luther King Jr. Culture Committee meeting, the Gardena Holly Park Homeowners
  Association meeting, and the Region 18 meeting of the Los Angeles County Democratic
  Party. She just wanted to say that the folks that attended the meeting at Nakaoka were
  very impressed with our facilities, they said it was very nice and the staff was wonderful
  so she wanted to thank the staff for everything. She visited the Wall That Heals and she’s
  glad we had another opportunity to see it because she thinks it’s important that we
  remember the men and women that made the ultimate sacrifice for our country. She said
  the number of people lost to that war is overwhelming to her and she just thinks of all the
  empty chairs at the dinner table across the years and children that won’t get to see
  grandparents and she hopes and prays that we never have to go through that type of
  war again. To our Vietnam veterans she thanked them for their service and sacrifice.
  She, too, wanted to give a special thank you and shout out to everyone that supported
  her re-election for her second term to Gardena City Council and she’s had some long
  conversations on what they can do to continue to make Gardena a great city to live, work,
  and play.

  11
 DocuSign Envelope ID: 394589BE-3E9A-431E-82D9-5B6716582723

  3) COUNCIL MEMBER TANAKA – Since their last gathering he attended our Finance
  Committee meeting with the city and he wanted to thank Mr. Beeman, our City Attorney
  and the staff that put the presentation on, it just shows what forward thinking minds we
  have when it comes to the finances of our city, so he thanked all of them for keeping us
  in the black. He attended the COG’s General Assembly at the Carson Community Center
  and he gave a thank you to Mayor Pro Tem Henderson for a great job moderating that.
  The keynote speaker was Congressional Member Ted Lieu and he believes this was the
  best General Assembly that they’ve put on since he’s been a part of the COG and said
  it’s going to be a hard shoe to fill next year, but they’re working on it. He attended the
  Battle of the Badges blood drive, and thanked Chief Saffell and his staff for putting that
  on, as well as the retirement ceremony for Officer Villanueva, he said it was well
  deserved for all the things he has done as an officer for this city and all the people that
  he’s touched, especially the young people in our schools so congratulations. He was
  honored to be asked to attend the Wall That Heals event that started at Mar Vista School
  in El Segundo, they asked him to pray for that wall and its journey through El Segundo
  to Gardena and he was very touched that he was asked to do that. He said it was a great
  event to pay tribute to 58,000 fallen on that wall, some that he went to high school with
  are on that wall. He continued by thanking all the veteran motorcycle groups, California
  Highway Patrol and members of the Gardena Police Department that escorted that wall
  from El Segundo to Johnson Park and he wanted to thank the city staff and the volunteers
  that watched over that wall for 24 hours a day for the days it was at Johnson Park just
  making sure it was safe and allowing people to come any time of the day or night just to
  visit. It was a tribute that he appreciated people going to and he thanked all the veterans
  and their families for the service to our country and he said the Gold Star Family that did
  a presentation there was totally touching and he doesn’t think there was a dry eye in the
  place, once again he said thank you all for your service and God bless you. He attended
  the Gardena Police foundation scholarship event, it was a great event to see all the kids
  with above 5.0 GPAs going to great schools and it’s good to see our Police Foundation
  supporting our youth to become future leaders in our communities. He attended the COG
  Steering Committee meeting and Director Stephany Santin and her staff were
  commended for a visit that they made regarding our senior services and the things that
  we put on, they were totally amazed at how many events that our city puts on for our
  seniors and he believes Stephany is going to be asked to be showcased by other cities
  coming here and seeing what she does so he thanked her for representing us as the
